utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in and around this courtroom. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case IT-09-92-T, the Prosecutor versus Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. There are no preliminaries announced. There is, however, one matter which I would like to deal with very briefly in private session. Could we move into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have difficulties in asking to return into open session because the issue was that it's uncertain whether we are in private session, but at least we'll continue in open session. Let's give it another try. We move now into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. While we're waiting for the witness to be escorted into the courtroom, I would like to briefly deal with another matter, that is the Prosecution tendered yesterday, the 26th of May, document 9821 as marked by the witness and that document was given number P6533, but the sacred words that "it is admitted into evidence" do not appear on the transcript. P6533 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Gengo. Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I apologise for interrupting, Your Honour. I just wanted to inform the Court, in line with our earlier discussions about Rule 90(E), this witness has received an admonishment previously in the Karadzic case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And the Chamber being aware of it leaves it in the hands of the Defence whether or not to ask for a 90(E) notice. Mr. Gengo, good morning. Apologies for letting you wait for a minute. Before you give evidence, the Rules require that you make a solemn declaration. The text is now handed out to you. May I invite you to make that solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Gengo. Please be seated. Mr. Gengo, you'll first be examined by Mr. Lukic. You'll find Mr. Lukic to your left. Mr. Lukic is counsel for Mr. Mladic. Mr. Lukic, you may proceed. Mr. Mladic, if we instruct the witnesses to refrain from any greetings, you should do the same. Is that clear to you? No loud speaking, Mr. Mladic. Mr. Lukic, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Gengo.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO GENGO
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we have in e-court Mr. Gengo's statement. It is 1D1600.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you see it before you on the screen?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO GENGO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you remember having given a statement to General Mladic's Defence team?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO GENGO
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: First I'd like to go to paragraph 20, which is something you pointed out previously. That is page 4 in the B/C/S. We have it at the top of the page in the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There were some typos pointed out by the witness yesterday. The PAT stands for anti-aircraft guns and they should be 20-millimetre in calibre rather than 21 as stated in the statement. Hence, instead of "21," the statement should reflect "20."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, where's PAT in paragraph 20?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It says here "heavy machine-guns," so in B/C/S it's "PAT." And for mortars it should say "60-millimetres" for the first one, not "62." Is there a need for me to read the whole paragraph corrected for the transcript?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If the witness -- does the witness have a hard copy of the statement?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Not in front of him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Not in front of him. Perhaps --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But he can see it on the screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, he can -- if you read it, Mr. Lukic, perhaps the relevant lines, that's okay then.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, we do have a hard copy if it would assist.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If need be, later we could provide it. But could you read the corrected lines, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And could you also give the context in which they appear. It's paragraph 20.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's paragraph 20. First sentence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I will read in B/C/S so Mr. Gengo can hear it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Gengo, I will read out the corrected version and please tell us if it is correct. In other words, the paragraph should read as follows: "The unit opposing -- the opposing unit from the ABiH possessed all kinds of infantry weapons: Heavy machine-guns; 20/1 mm, 20/2 mm, and 20/3 mm, and they mostly fired from the Jajce barracks (Mauritana [phoen] Pasino Brdo); they had a Zis 76-millimetre field gun which changed positions frequently; 60-millimetre, 82-millimetre, and 120-millimetre mortars frequently changed firing positions, especially the ones of smaller calibre." Does this reflect your corrections?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO GENGO
utterances.text: Yes, except for Zmajevac, you forgot Zmajevac which was a forward warehouse post of the Jajce military post in Alipasino Polje.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, you didn't only leave out Zmajevac, you left out the 1st Corps of the BH Army. I just want to correct that because --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: -- because otherwise we could form the impression that the witness corrected that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Also, Mr. Lukic, you said to us a few minutes ago that the 62 should change to 60.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Now when you read you said 62.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No, in transcript it's 60.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Well, I heard "62" in my ears.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you for your help.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Following these corrections, Mr. Gengo, I wanted to ask you whether everything is correctly entered in your statement?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO GENGO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If I were to ask you the same questions today, would you answer in the same way?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO GENGO
utterances.text: Yes, fully.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, it would be helpful if you would ask the witness if he signed this statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we see the first page of 1D1600.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Gengo, you see the document on the screen. Is that your signature?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO GENGO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we go to the last page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you see your signature before you on the last page of your statement?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO GENGO
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it clearly.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'd like to thank Judge Fluegge for reminding me. I would now like to tender Mr. Gengo's statement together with the accompanying documents to be entered into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: No objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The statement, document 1D1600, receives number D473, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Associated Exhibit 1D2060 receives number D474, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 1D2061 receives number D475, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: And document 1D2062 receives number D476, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Also admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I would read now, Your Honours, with your leave a summary of the statement of Mr. Gengo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please do so, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness Gengo was a member of the 1st Romanija Infantry Brigade of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps, situated at Spicaste Stijene. The witness will testify that ABiH snipers were firing upon civilians along the Vogosca-Hresa-Pale road. He will testify that the only war objective of the VRS in Sarajevo was to protect their own people, territory, and did not involve any offensive attacks against the army of B&H in Sarajevo. Army of B&H forces surrounded the VRS in the Sarajevo battle-field. ABiH forces fired from mobile launchers and other weapons mounted on vehicles, including to provoke return fire. ABiH military forces positioned themselves amongst settlements which were continuously inhabited by civilians. UNPROFOR was informed of cease-fire violations and fire from civilian facilities by the ABiH. All the mortars in the battalion of the witness only had co-ordinates for fire upon the line of confrontation. VRS units returned fire when fired upon, exclusively against enemy combat positions. Neither he nor his unit had any intention to cause civilian casualties or terrorise civilians who were under the control of the Muslim authorities. They were informed about the basic provisions of international law of war and humanitarian law through reports, orders, and the media. When required, the higher levels of command would issue orders of various forms of bans with the aim of respecting international law standards. On the 5th February, 1994, day of Markale I incident, he was in the command of the battalion in Hresa, 7 kilometres from Mrkovici. He did not hear any mortar activity nor did anyone report on that fact from his battalion. He was informed that an inspection team would come from the VRS Main Staff, the SRK, and the brigade command, escorted by UNPROFOR. The artillery pieces were not moved from their established firing positions before, during, or after the incident at Markale market. The inspections following the Markale I incident established that VRS positions did not fire upon Markale market. The average distance of the Muslim and Serbian lines were around 100 metres. Muslim forces would fire at passenger buses, civilian cars, and everything else that travelled along the Vogosca-Hresa-Pale road. The VRS provided security for the Mostanica spring water-supply line, made UNPROFOR's access possible and that of the teams from Sarajevo, in order to do checks and repairs. Water-supply was never deliberately switched off. That was summary of the statement of Mr. Gengo, and I would have several questions for him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please put them to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I would ask for the Exhibit P3 to put on our screens. [Interpretation] It is from the Sarajevo binder. We need page 30 in the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Gengo, we see a photograph. Do you recognise the place depicted?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO GENGO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What is before us?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO GENGO
utterances.text: The settlement of Sedrenik.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: On the left-hand side and in the centre of the photograph?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO GENGO
utterances.text: Spicaste Stijene.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Where is it exactly?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO GENGO
utterances.text: Here in this upper part.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I think it reads "Spicaste Stijene" as well?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO GENGO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: To the left, the TV repeater?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO GENGO
utterances.text: Yes, it is in the direction of the settlement of Grdonj.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You mention sniping in paragraph 29 of your statement --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: 39 of your statement.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You also said that it was impossible to engage in -- engage them because of the distance and the lie of the land?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO GENGO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In this photograph can we see your positions?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO GENGO
utterances.text: No, because they were behind sharp stone, Spicaste Stijene, on the other side of the hill.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know if everyone in the courtroom has the same photograph as me on the screen. Yes, it seems to be the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Explain to us briefly where were the positions and how far behind the hill were they?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO GENGO
utterances.text: Well, they were on the other side of the hill by some 10 metres away from the ridge.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The positions at Spicaste Stijene, were they exposed to enemy fire?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO GENGO
utterances.text: The positions at Spicaste Stijene were exposed to enemy fire from the left-hand side, from the repeater station, and from the right-hand side our forces were exposed to snipers. That is why we had to dig connecting trenches which still exist today in order to approach the front trench. The personnel in the trench could only defend themselves by using hand-grenades and nothing else because they couldn't see anything ahead. They attacked us by coming to the ridge of Spicaste Stijene and fired mortars and LPGs, hand-held rocket-launchers, the so-called Zoljas and Osas, thus placing our positions in danger. It so happened that they took three of our trenches at Spicaste Stijene by doing so. After that, once we regained them again, we were forced to strengthen our positions and place barbed wire and a wire fence to serve as a safety net of sorts against their shells so that they wouldn't ultimately reach our trenches. The snipers also engaged us. I remember a soldier who went to pick some cherries 100 metres from the trench line and they hit him through the neck because they had very up-to-date sniper rifles, which we didn't have. It was very difficult for us to extract his body, but unfortunately for him it was too late. He was dead on the spot. His name was Goran Tomic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Today if somebody were to be in your positions and if there was no danger of enemy fire, would they be able to fire at Sedrenik from either sniper or rifle?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO GENGO
utterances.text: No, we had M-76 snipers, 7.9-millimeters, and their range is up to 800 metres in ideal conditions. Since the elevation point Spicaste Stijene and Sedrenik were at 850 metres above the ground and the distance between them was over 1.000 metres, it was impossible and there was no line of visibility. A sniper shooter would have to come to the edge of Spicaste Stijene in order to see Sedrenik.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I just see on page 12, line 6 that the calibre of the bullets might not have been recorded. I believe the witness did say it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you repeat what the type of weapon was that had a range up to 800 metres in ideal conditions. It was an M-76 and then... ?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Just the calibre.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO GENGO
utterances.text: 7.9-millimetre.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I also noticed that some other figures have not been recorded properly so we will have to repeat.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What was the distance in height?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO GENGO
utterances.text: 250 metres between Sedrenik and Spicaste Stijene.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And what was the distance between them?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO GENGO
utterances.text: 1.350 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now this has been corrected.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, could we ask the witness to describe in detail what he considers to be Sedrenik because looking at maps it is about streets, it's about an area, it's -- and of course the best would be to have a detailed map of that area which is not to be found in P3 because Spicaste Stijene is not indicated on the maps specifically dealing with sniping incidents. So we could measure them on a map once the witness has further detailed his answer. Could you tell us what you consider to be comprised? Perhaps on this photograph to start with, what is Sedrenik, where does it begin?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sedrenik is a settlement or a neighbourhood. You can see it in this photo. And the elevation point is the crossroad in Sedrenik of the road that leads to the barracks from Kosevo and that is the crossroads at which the distance was measured.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me see. Could you be more precise in telling us exactly what crossroads?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't see it here; however, we are talking about a crossroads of several asphalt roads -- actually, those were village roads.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Is there any way that you could point at where that approximately is on this photograph? For example, I see a mosque with a -- a white mosque somewhere in the lower right part. Is that starting with the --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, I can see that. And it would be somewhere around there. You can see the road leading up to seven forests, and the crossroads is somewhere over there but you can't see it because of the angle from which the photo was taken. The roads come from this direction and from this direction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now you see there's also a marking on that map with an arrow which seems to be added to it F16 which seems to be also a smaller settlement. Would that also be part of Sedrenik?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, all of that was called Sedrenik. There may have been some smaller neighbourhoods or settlements, but all of them comprise Sedrenik.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes and are -- is the distance from there to Spicaste Stijene, is that the same or is it different?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It depended on the point from which measure. It can be more or less. If you're measuring from the crossroads, it's 450 metres. If you're measuring from a house which is further away, then the distance would be greater. So it all depended on the point from which you start measuring.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And you said it's 450 metres from -- that you had measured -- from the crossroads. From -- 450 metres from Spicaste Stijene to that crossroad; is that 450 metres?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, 1.350 metres, a mistake.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So the distance between Spicaste Stijene and Sedrenik very much depends on what point in Sedrenik you choose for the measurement; is that well understood?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And you mentioned 1.350 metres. I think earlier I heard "850," but perhaps I was -- oh, yes, I see now, it's page 13. Please proceed, Mr. Lukic, but for distances it appears that for the Chamber to fully understand the evidence we might need a bit more details on maps.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Gengo, were you on the site with the Karadzic team?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO GENGO
utterances.text: Yes. There was a girl called Nadja, I believe, as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It doesn't really matter who the team members were. But why did you take measurements and how come you measured 1.350 metres?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness and the counsel be alerted to the fact that they have to be interpreted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second. Mr. Gengo, you should take a short break between question and answer, otherwise the interpreters cannot interpret in a language we understand what you say. Mr. Weber is on his feet as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: If Mr. Lukic could please assist the Prosecution with directing us to where this information about a visit to the site is discussed by the witness and the particular measurements that were taken.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, could you include that perhaps in your questioning.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When we talked recently, did you point out the fact to me? Did you tell me that you were on the site with the Karadzic team?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO GENGO
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And did you also tell me that you took measurements from the instant at a certain address? This was not recorded. From which point did you take measurements at Spicaste Stijene?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO GENGO
utterances.text: It was number 156 in Sedrenik. I don't know which house it is, but its number is 156. In the indictment it says that a young girl was injured by sniper there, and when we took measurements it was 1.350 metres and the difference in height was 250 metres.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: If during the next break we could get a little bit more information about this. I do not see it a part of the proofing note or any information that's been disclosed to the Prosecution. If we could have some further information about just what exactly happened.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, you are asking questions about it, so I take it that you have been informed about from what house it was measured.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I was informed from number 156.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And which house is that? Are you serious in telling us that you don't know what house that is? So you are presenting evidence about a house of which you are not aware of which house it is, and then you expect us to draw any conclusions from that? Is that the position of the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I didn't want to enter into so much details, but Your Honour, [Indiscernible] -- all the details we now had to ask the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: General, sweeping statements do not make good evidence. So to say you could fire or you could not fire without knowing what we are talking about -- I mean, these details are vital, also for the Defence I would say. Therefore, at least the witness told you about an incident with a little girl. Did you verify which incident he was talking about?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: He was talking about the incident in connection with number 156 on Sedrenik.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but is that one -- he talks about an incident in the indictment. Did you verify which one it is? Is it in our indictment? Is it not? I see only one -- I see F16 in our case appearing prominently. Did you verify whether it's the same or whether it's a different one?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I think we have only one incident from Sedrenik.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's -- but is that the same one or is it a different one?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, the Chamber wouldn't mind if you would take the Defence seriously. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The witness didn't know the name of the [Overlapping speakers] and I couldn't clarify --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The witness gives his evidence what he observed, what he knows. You're in charge of the Defence to put that in context, to make that information for the Chamber on which it can rely if it has to make any determinations in this case. You can't say the witness -- of course the witness is just here to tell us what he knows; you should put it in context. It's your Defence case. And to say a measurement of 1350 metres, not knowing what house we are talking about. When there's one sniping incident in Sedrenik, the first that comes to your mind is: Would that be the distance between Spicaste Stijene and the -- where this incident happened? Is the witness talking about the same incident, yes or no? Or the same location which is related to the incident? I mean, these are the basic, primary questions that immediately come to anyone's mind who is preparing a defence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. And now I would like to call up 1D2037 in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Gengo, this is a document in English. It was drafted on the 5th of February, 1994. It is a letter sent by General Milovanovic. We already read it during your preparation for this testimony. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO GENGO
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Under 1 it says to: "Establish immediately a mixed expert military commission of the representatives of UNPROFOR, the Army of the Republika Srpska, and the so-called Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina ..." That was a proposal to UNPROFOR. Do you remember from back then that there were such intentions? Was that commission ever established? Did somebody come to visit your unit?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO GENGO
utterances.text: At that time, I don't remember there was a mixed commission of any kind, including Muslim forces, UNPROFOR, and our representatives; however, there was a commission that arrived on the 6th of February and visited the positions of the 7th Battalion. There were also the representatives of the 1st Romanija Brigade, the representatives of the corps, and the representatives of the Main Staff. They arrived around 10.00. I sent them my security officer who was in charge of co-operating with UNPROFOR and I asked him to take them to Mrkovici. They went there on that day, they spent about three hours there, they returned, and the officer reported to me about what had transpired; and then they left. I don't know where they went.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, this is all in the statement; you are aware of that?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I just want to enter this document --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- into the evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's fine. But if you have any additional questions --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- then please make something new. Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: No objection, but just if we could clarify: With respect to this document, there are references to 6 January 1994. It's the Prosecution's understanding that that's just a typographical error, that should be the 6th of February, 1994. I don't know if the Defence has the same understanding of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Exactly, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, so the parties do agree that the reference to the 6th of January in this document which dates from the 5th of February, 1994, is a mistake and should read "February."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Could we have a look on the last page of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, can we have the last page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is there -- is another typo, then, Mr. Weber, I take it on the second page where it talks about the 5th of January which in the context should also be understood as the 5th of February, 6.00 in the afternoon to receive a response. The parties do agree on that as well?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: What about item 5, last line, January 7, 1994; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Yes, as Your Honours have already noted that in the context of the date of this letter, I believe that the reading should more likely be that it's referring to February, not January.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Everything -- the author of this document was one month behind.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: With this understanding, Madam Registrar, the number would be?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 1D2037 receives number D477, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D477 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let me just ask you briefly. You said that BiH army did not represent -- accept to be members of the commission. On that occasion, did the Serbian side try to hide anything?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO GENGO
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you see an order, were you verbally ordered to remove or destroy any evidence before that visit?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO GENGO
utterances.text: No, nothing of the kind happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Without any order, did you still try to conceal something?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO GENGO
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You told us that Muslims opened fire from civilian populated areas. Was there an obligation for Muslim forces to remove civilians from which they launch assault operations?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO GENGO
utterances.text: Yes, there was an obligation on their part to do that; it was their duty.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The rules of the former JNA, did they envisage such a thing, i.e., that civilians should be removed from the area from which attacks were launched?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO GENGO
utterances.text: Yes, civilians had to be protected in any case and in any way.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Gengo. This was all I had for you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Lukic. Mr. Weber, are you ready to cross-examine the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, if I could just have one second.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Gengo, you'll now be cross-examined by Mr. Weber. You'll find him to your right and Mr. Weber is counsel for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Gengo. Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO GENGO
utterances.text: Good morning. I can hear you very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I just want to start today with some basic questions before the next break. They relate to your brigade. In your statement you indicate that you were a member of the 216th JNA Mountain Brigade in 1991. Is it correct that the 216th Mountain Brigade was part of the JNA 4th Corps?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO GENGO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Dragomir Milosevic was the commander of the 216th Mountain Brigade?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO GENGO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The headquarters of the 216th Mountain Brigade was located in Han Pijesak?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Is that a question, Mr. Weber?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: They are questions, Your Honour. If you'd like I can say --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It sounds like a statement of witness evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. If it's okay to proceed, I do believe the witness answered the last question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, and next question is phrased in a way that it also looks like a question.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have 65 ter 08603 for the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, coming up before you is a 4th Corps order to the command of the 216th Mountain Brigade dated 17 May 1992. I'd like to direct your attention to item 4 on the list which says: "216th Mountain Brigade is receiving the title: 1st Romanija Brigade ..." Is it correct that your brigade was renamed the 1st Romanija Brigade in May 1992?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO GENGO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Directing your attention to item 1, is it correct that this occurred at the same time that the 4th Corps was renamed the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO GENGO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Is it correct that with this redesignation you became a member of the Army of Republika Srpska in May 1992?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO GENGO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: In paragraph 2 of your statement, you indicate that you were the commander of the tactical maintenance weapons and ammunition workshop from 1991 until September 1992. Is it correct that you occupied the same position after the brigade was renamed?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO GENGO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Dragomir Milosevic -- excuse me, is it correct that Dragomir Milosevic also continued to serve as commander of the 1st Romanija Brigade until February 1993?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO GENGO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: After then-Colonel Milosevic was transferred to the Drina Corps, is it correct that Vlado Lizdek became the commander of the 1st Romanija Brigade?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO GENGO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: After this redesignation occurred in May 1992, is it correct that the headquarters of the 1st Romanija Brigade remained in Han Pijesak?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO GENGO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honours, at this time the Prosecution would tender this document and I'm about to head into another topic, if this is a good time for a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, the number would you please?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 8603 receives number P6534, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I hear of no objections, therefore admitted into evidence. We take a break now before we turn to a new area. Could the parties provide a map specifically of the Spicaste Stijene area and -- so that we have at least an opportunity to further verify -- of course preferably with houses numbers, but even if not the Chamber would like to be able to consider asking further questions about the matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Of course, Your Honour. And yesterday Mr. Groome used 65 ter 9821, which I believe is a detailed map; however, I looked on the electronic version on it and when you do zoom in it is difficult to see things. If it's okay with the Chamber, I can bring back enlarged hard copies of that map, if it would assist.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Whatever you have which might serve us. Of course it's important to be able to see whether -- where F16 is, if the parties could provide further information about an incident with a little girl which appears in the indictment, then of course we would be better able to understand the details of the evidence of this witness. We take a break, but not until after the witness has been escorted out of the courtroom. You may follow the usher, Mr. Gengo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And we resume at ten minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the witness be escorted into the courtroom. Mr. Lukic, could at any point in time could we have a closer look at D474, 475, and 476, because the marking seems not to be very clear. Perhaps you could first already yourself have a look at it. These are the associated exhibits.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Gengo, is it correct that you were in Han Pijesak from May until September 1992?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO GENGO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Is it correct that you were in Han Derventa between September 1992 and January 1994?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO GENGO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: During that time - so I'm speaking between May 1992 and January 1994 - is it correct that you were not involved in the planning of any operations as a battalion commander?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO GENGO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Is it correct that you are not familiar with the operations carried out by your brigade during your time in Han Pijesak and Han Derventa between May 1992 and January 1994?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO GENGO
utterances.text: Yes, partially.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: When you say "yes, partially," is it correct that you for the most part are not familiar with the operations that were carried out during your time in Han Pijesak and Han Derventa?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO GENGO
utterances.text: Yes, because I was involved in logistics and for the most part I was not familiar with any of that because I was on field missions.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Right. So aside from your role in logistics, you would not be familiar with the operations of your brigade during that time?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO GENGO
utterances.text: I said "yes, partially," but I didn't know everything.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, did you -- is it correct that you provided or you attended an interview with members of the Office of the Prosecutor on 16 October 2012?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO GENGO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, I want to read you one of your answers during that interview and ask you if you stand by it. This is at page 23 of the interview transcript. "At the time I was the commander of the battalion and what happened during that, I was responsible for that" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Can we have that on the screen?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Of course, Your Honours. It's uploaded as 65 ter 30671, e-court page 23. And to assist Your Honours, I believe it's towards the bottom of the page from lines 27 and onward starting with the answer at line 30.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, in response to a question you stated: "At the time I was the Commander of the Battalion. And what happened during that I was responsible for that. Everything what took place ... had taken place before or what took place after, I don't know what happened before or after me." Do you stand by this statement?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO GENGO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'd like to move on now to actually discussing your time as battalion commander. In paragraphs 3 and 4 of your statement you indicate that you were a battalion commander between January 1994 and February 1995. My first question is: Did you become a battalion commander in early or late January 1994?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO GENGO
utterances.text: No. It was in early February. I can't remember the exact date. I believe that it was on the 27th of January. There must be an order to that effect. There is an order, as a matter of fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay. I just want to ask you a couple of things just so we have a clear record. In your last answer you said: "It was in early February." And then you indicated you couldn't remember the date. And then you said you believe it was on the 27th of January. Do you maintain your evidence that you became a battalion commander in January 1994?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO GENGO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Do I correctly then understand your evidence that you believe it was sometime toward the end of January 1994?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO GENGO
utterances.text: Yes -- huh?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, did you say something? I'm sorry, the transcript did not record you?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO GENGO
utterances.text: No, no, no, I didn't say anything. I said that I stand by the fact that it was in late January 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, sir. During your time as battalion commander, is it correct that there were over 800 men subordinated to you?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO GENGO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Is it correct that there were at least 650 men in the infantry companies of your battalion?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO GENGO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Is it correct that there were 15 men in the communications section of your battalion?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO GENGO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Is it correct that you maintained communications with the brigade command; the Kosevo Brigade, your neighbouring brigade to the west; and the 4th Mixed Artillery Regiment?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO GENGO
utterances.text: Yes, but the Kosevo unit was a battalion, not a brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Thank you for that clarification. It was a part of a different brigade than your own; correct?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO GENGO
utterances.text: It was under the command of the 3rd Sarajevo unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Is it correct that your communications functioned well?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO GENGO
utterances.text: For the most part.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Is it correct that the commander of the 4th Mixed Artillery Regiment, also known as MAP, was Radislav Cvjetkovic?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO GENGO
utterances.text: Radislav Cvjetkovic was his name.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Is it correct that there was a mortar platoon consisting of 36 or 37 men subordinated to you?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO GENGO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Is it correct that the mortars could not be used without your authorisation?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO GENGO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Did the mortar crews ever fire without your approval?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO GENGO
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Is it correct that you needed to seek authorisation from your superior command in order to fire your mortars?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO GENGO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And in turn, your superior command could only authorise the firing of a mortar with the approval of the commander of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO GENGO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Is it correct that there were 82- and 120-millimetre mortars were positioned to face targets located inside the inner ring of Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO GENGO
utterances.text: On the positions of the enemy side, and co-ordinates were given for those positions -- for the defence of our positions, that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, please listen to my question carefully. Those positions were located inside the inner ring of Sarajevo; correct?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO GENGO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your mortar crews could not see into the city from their positions; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO GENGO
utterances.text: That is correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Is it correct that each of your mortar crews possessed a firing table at every mortar location?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO GENGO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: In your statement you describe different weapons and projectiles used by the ABiH. Is it correct that they fired these projectiles from the Jajce barracks and a forward position located outside of town in Pasino Brdo?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO GENGO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: When you were firing a 120-millimetre mortar round from Mrkovici toward these locations, is it correct that the distance travelled by those projectiles would be in the range of 3 to 4 kilometres?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO GENGO
utterances.text: It depended on the target.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Well, sir, I'm asking specifically from your positions in Mrkovici to the Jajce barracks or Pasino Brdo, is it correct that the range would be approximately 3 to 4 kilometres?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO GENGO
utterances.text: Yes, approximately.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I would like to discuss with you some other locations. You've mentioned that some areas you were aware of were inhabited by civilians. Is it correct that the areas facing your battalion from inside the inner ring were inhabited by civilians?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO GENGO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Is it correct that this included the area known as Sedrenik?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO GENGO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Is it correct that this also included the slopes of Grdonj?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO GENGO
utterances.text: Slopes of Grdonj, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: During your time as a battalion commander, you knew these areas contained private houses and family homes; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO GENGO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Is it correct that the city centre was also a residential area?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO GENGO
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, that's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: During direct examination you were asked some general questions about precautions relating to civilians. I'd like to more specifically ask you: What precautions did you take to minimise civilian casualties when firing?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO GENGO
utterances.text: I did not understand your question. Could you please repeat? I don't know what answer you expect from me.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Of course. When you were authorising your subordinates to fire, what precautions did you take to minimise civilian casualties?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO GENGO
utterances.text: But what side did you have in mind? Did you have in mind the opposing side or my own side?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I have in mind you.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO GENGO
utterances.text: Please repeat.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'll ask again. When you were authorising your subordinates to fire, what precautions did you take to minimise civilian casualties?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: The witness wanted to know if you are referring to civilians of the opposing side or of the own side.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: You should clarify that in your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Well, what I'm talking about, sir, is civilian casualties that could result as a consequence of your firing. So wherever you were firing to, what precautions did you take to minimise civilian casualties?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just to be clear, Mr. Weber, are you talking of perhaps firing at Jajce barracks or Pasino Brdo?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'm talking about whenever he was authorising his subordinates to fire, what precautions did he take to minimise civilian casualties in those areas that were being targeted.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When it comes to my side, I did not have anything to discuss with the opposing side. If the opposing side opened mortar fire on my positions and it was done -- and if it was done from a mobile mortar, they were supposed to secure that place to make sure that the returning shell would not hit civilians because they were a legitimate military target for me. A mortar that was placed either in front of a school or in the middle of a settlement was a military legitimate target. It was not up to me to try and see what surrounded. It was the opposing side that was supposed to do that in order to avoid civilian casualties. All I could do was to target well so there was no dissipation of fragments, an unnecessary dissipation of fragments.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: You said a number of things just there.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO GENGO
utterances.text: What is it that you want me to say?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: If you could wait for my question, please. Is it correct that you did not take any precautions, that you merely left it up to the opposing side; is that your evidence?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO GENGO
utterances.text: What was I supposed to do on the opposing side? I couldn't do anything, could I? I could not really remove their own civilians away from their pieces, from their weapons.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we just try to clarify matters. Do I understand your testimony well that you authorised firing exclusively if you had been fired at and that the target was the origin of the fire that targeted you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And do I understand your testimony well that if that fire came from an area which was inhabited possibly by civilians, that the measure you took was to be as precise in hitting your target as you possibly could but that if civilians would be hit in that area, that you considered that to be a responsibility of the opposite party?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, because in that case they would be collateral damage, not a specific target.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber, that's apparently the evidence of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: May I put a follow-up question to the witness. Sir, some minutes ago you said - this is to be found on page 30, line 10 to 12 - Mr. Weber put to you: "Your mortar crews could not see into the city from their positions; is that correct?" And your answer was: "That is correct, yes." How were you able to distinguish the target between civilian settlements and the positions of mortars directed to you without being able to see the inner city?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There were places from which you could see it. For example, across from the area of Borije and we could see their positions from ours and the crews would let us know where they were. There were observers reporting on which parts the fire was coming from. However, the crew on its own could not do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, I'm going to read you an answer you provided during the interview on the 16th of October, 2012.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, for reference this is on page 29 of 30671.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: During that interview you stated: "Hand-grenades are not like a pear that you can put it in a bag or here or there. As you know, it explodes and shrapnel have wider domain causing injuries. So it was inevitable that the civilians would get hurt as well." Do you stand by that statement?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO GENGO
utterances.text: Not hand-grenades but mines. No one can throw a hand-grenade 1300 metres far.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, if I could clarify. I actually believe -- is it correct that you're referring to mortars, "grenata"?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO GENGO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber, you used the term "hand-grenades."

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I appreciate it. I was just reading directly from the hand-grenades, but I appreciate the witness's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: In the transcript there is no reference to hand-grenades but to grenades.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: With that clarification, do you stand by that statement?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO GENGO
utterances.text: I stand by the fact that there were mortar shells which were hitting a space of 50 square metres. Whoever was inside that area may have been hurt.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Is it correct that you knew that it was inevitable that civilians would be hurt?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO GENGO
utterances.text: If they were inside the area, it was normal to expect that they might become injured by pieces of shrapnel.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: In paragraph 23 of your statement, you state: "Potential victims among the civilians could be considered collateral damage." Is it correct that this is how you viewed the Muslim population living in the areas you shelled?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO GENGO
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I didn't fully understand the question, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, there was no intentional targeting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. For collateral damage of course there is no intentional targeting. That is what is in the definition of "collateral damage." But I didn't fully understand your question, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: When you say potential victims among the civilians, are the civilians that you're referring to the Muslim population that lived inside the inner ring?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Could you answer the question?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: In your statement when you say potential victims among the civilians, are the civilians that you're referring to the Muslim population that lived inside the inner ring?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO GENGO
utterances.text: There were Serb inhabitants, Croat inhabitants, and others. I don't know who could have been there. The question is not completely clear to me. There was no way for me to know.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Then should we understand you mean generally the population living inside the inner ring?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO GENGO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Now, in paragraph 27 of your statement you state that: "We informed UNPROFOR about every instance of abuse with regard to the deployment of military targets, fire from civilian facilities, and cease-fire violations." Is it then correct that the United Nations Military Observers, or UNMOs, in Sarajevo would have possessed information regarding the activities of the SRK?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO GENGO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Is it correct that units of the SRK regularly shelled the city centre and Sedrenik?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO GENGO
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have P4610 for the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Gengo, coming up before you here is a UNMO sitrep dated 26 December 1993. It's covering the period between the 25th to the 26th. I'd like to direct your attention to the part of the sitrep that states: "The tension in Sarajevo decreased but the city still remains unstable. There was reduced activity during the whole day. The activity was mainly in the CFL," confrontation lines, "areas. 70 per cent of the total impacts. The residential areas shelled today were the city centre as always, the area of Sedrenik," and then there's other areas that are listed. Then just so we have a little bit more of a picture here, I'd like to direct your attention down on the report a little bit to under section 2, which I believe you can see on the B/C/S version. It states: "UNMOs confirm the following: Bosnian incoming - 266 mixed impacts, Bosnian outgoing 2 explosions, Serb incoming 34 mixed impacts, Serb outgoing 108 mixed rounds ..." I just want to make sure we're clear about a couple of things before we start discussing some items. Do you understand that this report indicates that the UNMOs observed 266 impacts in ABiH territory and 34 impacts in the area of the SRK?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO GENGO
utterances.text: Yes, depending on the degree of their objectivity in reporting those figures --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, I just want to make sure we have some understanding on some facts and then we'll discuss it a little bit further. Do you also understand that on this date the UNMOs observed 108 outgoing rounds from the SRK and two outgoing rounds from the ABiH?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO GENGO
utterances.text: Yes, if they were objective and I don't think they were. I don't think these figures are realistic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I take it from the "they" you're referring to UNMOs?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO GENGO
utterances.text: Yes, yes, whether they recorded it all properly.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, let's go on the information that's here. There's evidence in this case --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And for Your Honours this is referring to transcript page 5470.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: -- that mixed impacts refer to the possible combination of tank, mortar, and artillery rounds. I'd like to just go one by one with these. Could you tell us which SRK brigades were able to target Sedrenik with their tanks?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO GENGO
utterances.text: Perhaps from the sector of Trebevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Yes. And what brigade and battalion would that be?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO GENGO
utterances.text: The Trebevic Battalion of the 1st Romanija Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Which SRK brigades were able to target Sedrenik with their mortars?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO GENGO
utterances.text: Again, the 1st Romanija Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Which SRK brigades were able to target Sedrenik with their artillery?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO GENGO
utterances.text: Well, it could have been the 4th MAP.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Yes, and could you please tell us the types of artillery they had.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO GENGO
utterances.text: They had 155-millimetre howitzers, they had 122-millimetre assets, and they had I think a 130-millimetre cannon.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Is it correct that the 4th MAP would operate in your zone of responsibility?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO GENGO
utterances.text: They had their positions in the area of Sreposko [phoen].

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Is it correct that the 4th MAP would operate in your zone of responsibility? If you could please be clear.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO GENGO
utterances.text: They had their positions behind my back because they were supposed to provide us with support.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'd like to move on to the other residential area that's discussed in this UNMO report. Which SRK brigades were able to target the city centre with their tanks?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO GENGO
utterances.text: Only the 1st Sarajevo unit and the Igman -- no, not the Igman unit but the Ilidza unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And when you say the 1st Sarajevo unit, are you referring to the 1st Sarajevo Mechanised Brigade?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO GENGO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And when you are referring - just so we have a clear understanding - to the Igman unit, you're referring to the Igman Brigade; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO GENGO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Which SRK brigades were able to target the city centre with their mortars?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO GENGO
utterances.text: The city centre, I don't know. It depended on their positions. I don't know where the mortar positions of the other units were.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay. How about for the 1st Romanija Brigade?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO GENGO
utterances.text: The 1st Romanija Brigade had mortar positions, as I mentioned. I told you where they were deployed in my unit. I don't know for other units.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Could the witness be asked to speak up. We barely hear him.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, if there's anything additional --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour, if you wanted to go ahead.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, could you please speak a bit louder and into the microphone so that the interpreters can hear you better.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And, sir, I'm not sure if we missed any part of your answer there, so if you could please repeat your answer to the last question. And if you don't remember it, I can repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO GENGO
utterances.text: Please do.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'll rephrase it slightly just so it's clear. With respect to the mortars of the 1st Romanija Brigade, is it correct that they were able to target the city centre with their mortars? And, sir, I'd remind you you've already said that they had an approximate range of 3 to 4 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO GENGO
utterances.text: Yes. I think I said I don't know where the mortars of other battalions were. I only knew where my mortars were.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I think your evidence is sufficiently clear on that. Which SRK brigades were able to target the city centre with their artillery?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO GENGO
utterances.text: Repeat, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Of course, sir. I'd be happy to. Which SRK brigades were able to target the city centre with their artillery?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO GENGO
utterances.text: Well, all save for the Igman and the Ilijas one.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And when you say "all," you're including the brigades that were directly attached at the corps level, such as the 4th MAP?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO GENGO
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution now please have P542 for the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Gengo, this is a UNMO sitrep for the evening of 4 February 1994, the night before the Markale shelling. The sitrep indicates: "Most impacts in the period of 1600 to 2359 hours on the 4th of February "seemed to be close to the confrontation line ...," and it lists a number of areas including an area east of city centre with a grid reference that is near Sedrenik. During this period the sitrep indicates that the BiH incoming were 64 mixed rounds and 14 anti-aircraft rounds and no BiH outgoing were seen or heard. Eight mixed BSA outgoing rounds were observed along with 50 anti-aircraft rounds. Is it correct that this sitrep shows that the SRK was firing on areas of Sarajevo and it was not in response to any incoming fire?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO GENGO
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO GENGO
utterances.text: These were legitimate military targets.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: -- that was not my question.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: If Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Is it correct that this sitrep shows that the SRK was firing on areas of Sarajevo and it was not in response to any incoming fire?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO GENGO
utterances.text: Well, I don't know about this report, but I don't think it was the case. We never opened fire from our positions without a good reason.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, you really haven't answered my question yet. I'll repeat it again. Is it correct --

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO GENGO
utterances.text: Please do.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Is it correct that this sitrep shows that the SRK was firing on areas of Sarajevo and it was not in response to any incoming fire?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We can read it from the document. This is not a question for the witness, Your Honour. I object to this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is a question for the witness, Mr. Lukic. Earlier we asked him a question about responding to incoming fire. Please, could you please answer the question. And it's relevant also in view of other evidence that we have heard. Could you please answer the question whether this document indicates that sometimes the -- that areas of Sarajevo were fired at without this firing being triggered by incoming fire?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is possible that their bunkers and fortifications were targeted. That's the only possibility. No one fired at the city and at civilians at random.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The question is whether this report indicates that even without incoming fire - and you may have had many reasons to do that - but whether it happened that you fired at targets without -- without that being a response to incoming fire?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Only if we were trying to improve our tactical position in order to deal with a certain part of territory so as to have the enemy withdraw further away from any roads. That's when it could have happened.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So the first answer is: Yes, it happened that you fired not in response to incoming fire but for other reasons, if I understood you well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could we please have the next page of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Gengo, this is the sitrep for the next morning on 5 February 1994. It lists that the areas that were shelled near the confrontation line and it then states: "... residential areas shelled were city centre ..." And: "UNMOs have confirmed the following: BiH in - 22 mixed impacts, BiH out - none observed, BSA in - none observed, BSA out - 3 mortar." Is it correct that this sitrep also shows that the SRK was firing and it was not in response to incoming fire?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO GENGO
utterances.text: Can I have the document? I can't see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, it should be appearing before you and it does. This is the sitrep for the next morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Can you see it, Witness? If it's not on your screen, the usher should assist.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Please let me know if you need to review the document. I'd be happy to repeat my question.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO GENGO
utterances.text: I've read the document. Please repeat your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Is it correct that this sitrep also shows that the SRK was firing and it was not in response to incoming fire?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO GENGO
utterances.text: I don't know if the report is objective as compiled by UNPROFOR and whether they reported on the correct figures regarding the other side.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, that doesn't answer my question. Is it correct that this sitrep also shows --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, the sitrep shows what the author of the sitrep has observed. Whether that happened or not is of course a different question. So if you say: Does the document show that this and this happened, then of course the witness is right in saying that it depends on the reliability of the observations by the authors of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But of course it would be a legitimate question to ask the witness that: If this is reported and whether he has an explanation for such a report, and you could ask these type of questions, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, is it correct that during this time that you were -- was this during the time-period in which you were located over 7 kilometres away from the front line on the 5th of February, 1994?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO GENGO
utterances.text: What do you mean 7 kilometres? Where did you find that number? I don't understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I believe in your statement you indicated that on the 5th of February, 1994, you were in Hresa, approximately 7 kilometres away from the front line.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO GENGO
utterances.text: Yes, the alleged conflict, but it wasn't really like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'll let the witness answer the question, but how I read this document, it does not distinguish the line -- first it enumerates areas and at the end it says --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- how many grenades.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, if you want to point to anything, then we should do that in the absence of the witness because we are guiding the witness on how to read the document, which of course is not -- if he -- do you understand any English, Mr. Gengo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please take off your earphones for a second.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: May I? Thank you. From this document it does not say whether those grenades were targeting -- it says CFL by conflict line or it's essential, so if we want to establish the distance we should know where exactly these shells were targeted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But I do understand that the distance had to do with where the witness was.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But it depends from the line or from the centre.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, how essential are the 7 kilometres?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I came away from the document to establish the witness's -- and I'm talking now outside the presence of the witness, to establish the whereabouts of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: To establish the fact he would not know anything to dispute this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And the witness says so in paragraph 40 of his own statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So I think the parties could agree on where that location is where the witness was at that time, and that apparently is the only thing you want to establish at this moment. Not many people can see at a distance of 7 kilometres. That's --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- or 5. Yes. Mr. Lukic, it's clear?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, "Svedok," could you -- yes. If I say "witness," he might not hear it without earphones, without translation. Then I'm also looking at the clock at this moment. Mr. Weber, perhaps we first ask the witness to take a break.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Of course, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: To be escorted out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, we do have some maps present, enlargements of the area that you requested.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: By the way, the 7th kilometres is in the statement, Hrasna, 7 kilometres from Mrkovici, not from the confrontation lines, not from the impact, but from Mrkovici. Yes, could you, if you would have those maps available, could I just have a very quick look at it so to see whether it serves our purpose. Oh, the usher is out. Perhaps the Chamber staff could exceptionally assist in giving it to Madam Registrar, who will then further distribute it. Yes, for the Defence as well. Yes. Mr. Lukic, we were a bit confused when you asked the witness questions about the measurement and I think you referred to a young girl appearing in the indictment. From what I see, the one and only sniping incident, if it is sniping, because the adjudicated facts say it's machine-gun fire, is F16.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And it's a boy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And it's a boy of 14 years old. So that's -- must be -- that measurement seems to be therefore pretty irrelevant for us.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I learned from the witness that he went in 2012 and led by Karadzic team to one location in Sedrenik.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes [overlapping speakers] --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- establish with him which incident so I couldn't go further with him. He knew the address in front of which they were and from where they measured.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, okay -- [overlapping speakers].

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I checked the statement, I checked the medical documents, I checked the police report, and I have the numbers here, but there is no address. So --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- with this witness I couldn't compare those data.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So I got from him what I could get from him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.
